caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular, double-door cabinet with ornate detailing. The doors are framed in green with hinges on the left and right edges. The top of the cabinet has an elaborate carved crest featuring a central shell motif surrounded by green vine-like patterns with red flowers and leaves. Each door panel is decorated with swirling green vines, red leaves, pomegranates, and small red diamond shapes, all against a beige background. The left door panel contains an image of a monstrance—a golden sunburst with a cross at its top, standing on a green and brown rectangular pedestal. The right door panel features a chalice with a round white host above it, also positioned on a similar pedestal. The entire composition uses earthy tones, predominantly brown, green, red, and gold, and the background outside the cabinet is a plain off-white. The artist’s signature, "V. Van Voris," appears in the lower right corner.
title: Hand-carved Cabinet
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
